label: D40a-mekanisme-provisioning-aman (eskalasi)
decision: How should POST /v1/enrollments/{id}/credentials prove that the request comes from the device that started the enrolment (ADR-0039), so that knowing a cred_id, the card instance id (returned by :challenge) or the device id is not enough to mint a credential?

candidates.description: The app generates a 32-byte provisioning secret per enrolment and sends its SHA-256 in POST /v1/enrollments (provisioning_key_hash). The server stores the hash on the card instance when the instance is created, and replaces it when the same device gets the instance back through an enrolment call (resume or promotion). Every POST /v1/enrollments/{id}/credentials must present the secret (Authorization: Bearer), compared in constant time; a missing or wrong secret is answered with the same 404 ENR-NOT-FOUND as an unknown id.

Like enrolment_secret_all for the first credential of a PROVISIONING instance; additionally, adding a channel to an ACTIVE instance requires a possession signature from an existing credential key of that instance (challenge nonce, message 'ANP1-ADD-CHANNEL' ‖ cred_id ‖ nonce ‖ channel), shown to the user as part of the add-channel action.

Reuse the status read token as the instance secret: its hash is sent at enrolment instead of at provisioning, and provisioning requires the status token as bearer. One secret per instance serves both reading status and provisioning.
Provisioning requires the body to contain the instance's device_id, and :challenge stops returning card_instance_id (the app relies on its stored serverCardID). No new secret.

priorities: 1) Knowing a cred_id, the card instance id, the device id or reader data must not allow provisioning. 2) No Face ID or passcode prompts outside actions the user started, and no raw secret persisted on the server (including idempotency rows). 3) Same-device resume (ADR-0034) and invitation promotion (ADR-0035) keep working. 4) Minimal API and app change.
requirements: An attacker who knows a cred_id, the card instance id and the device id, but has no data stored only on the enrolling device, cannot obtain a credential through POST /v1/enrollments/{id}/credentials.
Resuming an unfinished enrolment (ADR-0034) or promoting a pending one (ADR-0035) still lets the legitimate device provision its first credential.
No raw secret is stored on the server, including idempotency rows.
